options.why: Divided $625$ by $5$ instead of writing $625$ as a power of $5$.
Ignored that the right-hand side is a reciprocal, which makes the index negative.
Used the whole denominator as the index instead of writing $32=2^{5}$.
Made the index a fraction because the right-hand side is a fraction.
Formed $4x=3$ correctly but then divided the wrong way round.
Used the index of $27$ as the answer without dividing by the index of $81$.
Divided the bases, $27\div81$, instead of comparing the indices.
Missed that $\frac{1}{27}$ is $3^{-3}$ and solved $-x=3$ instead.
Took the reciprocal of the index rather than using a negative index.
Used the whole denominator as the index instead of writing $27=3^{3}$.
Expanded the left index as $10x+3$, multiplying only the $2x$ by $5$.
Used $128=2^{6}$ instead of $2^{7}$ when converting to the prime base.
Collected the $x$ terms on the wrong side, reversing the sign of the answer.
Treated $\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{x}$ as $4^{x}$, losing the negative index.
Wrote $\frac{1}{4}$ as $2^{-1}$ instead of $2^{-2}$ when changing base.
Took the reciprocal of the answer because the base was a reciprocal.
Inverted the fractional index, putting the root index on top.
Used the power of $36$ without dividing by the root index $3$.
Used the root index alone, ignoring that $36=6^{2}$.
Rewrote $0.2$ as $5$ rather than $\frac{1}{5}$, losing the reciprocal.
Used the denominator $5$ as the index instead of the index $-1$.
Set the index equal to the fraction $\frac{1}{5}$ itself.
Left $4^{-2x+1}$ as $2^{-2x+1}$, forgetting that $4=2^{2}$ doubles the index.
Used $32=2^{4}$ instead of $2^{5}$ when changing the right-hand side.
Subtracted the two indices instead of adding them when multiplying the powers.
Treated $36^{3+2n}$ as $6^{3+2n}$, forgetting that $36=6^{2}$ doubles the index.
Solved $3n+6=0$ but divided with the wrong sign.
Set the index itself equal to $-6$ instead of solving $3n+6=0$.
